experiments.name: t1_baseline_aa@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #1 baseline: the default bot, 1 seat vs 3x catanatron 3.3 ValueFunctionPlayer. Its default arm is the reference every later value experiment reuses (same arm key). Played as an A/A (candidate = default), so every pair must be identical (ident = pairs, delta exactly 0); anything else means nondeterminism and invalidates the pairing. Baseline s.e. about 1.1 pp at 2000 games. 4000 games at 6110 g/h (3 workers): 0.65 h.

experiments.name: t1_search_vs_heur@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #2: is the depth-1 search worth it vs catanatron? Candidate = the greedy heuristic bot (the search bot's own priors, no search). Default arm reused from t1_baseline_aa@value. Only 2000 heuristic games: estimated at 0.6x a search game (not measured), 0.19 h (0.33 h if as slow as the default).

experiments.name: t1_trades0_vrule@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #3: trade proposals 3 (default) vs 0, the self-play +17.5 pp result. Under --trades value, the only mode the verification judged honest: catanatron's own players never accept (value always rejects, alphabeta raises). Answers come from OUR value rule (accept iff the responder's own catanatron value function rises), so report this row as 'vs value-rule responders', never as 'vs Catanatron'. Own default arm (trading on); tier-2 trade rows reuse it. 2000 x (1.33 + 0.70) s = 1.13 h at 3550 g/h, less if the sequential stop fires.

experiments.name: t1_openings@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #4: the three opening policies vs the current search opening (default arm reused). setup_pick is the control: the current heuristic ranking forced without search in setup. Every non-current policy also switches the search off in setup, so read each policy against setup_pick as well; that contrast is the difference of the two rows on the same seeds (paired per seed from this JSONL). The lever targets seats 2-3: read the 'by seat' line of `ablate_catanatron.py --report --out <dir>/t1_openings@value.jsonl`. 8000 candidate games at 0.59 s: 1.31 h.

experiments.name: t1_depth2@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #5: de-noised depth 2 vs depth 1 against value (so far measured only vs our stand-ins: -1.7 +- 2.1 pp vs vf over 840 games). Default arm reused; the candidate is about 2.4x as slow (pilot: 4.0 vs 1.6-2.0 s/game). 2000 x 1.41 s = 0.78 h. Its ms/decision is compared against reused default games, which ran at another time and load (marked '(reused)').

experiments.name: t1_blockw0_pyeval@value
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #6: blockability weight 0 vs 1 (the self-play -1.7 pp was measured half-applied on the C++ evaluator). Needs the Python evaluator (re-exec with CATANBOT_NO_ACCEL=1), so both arms run about 3x slower and the C++ default arm cannot be reused. This experiment plays the Python-evaluator default arm that t2_exposure0_pyeval@value reuses. 4000 games at 1960 g/h: 2.04 h.

experiments.name: t1_baseline_aa@vf
experiments.notes: TIER 1 replicate on catanatron 3.2.1 vs our in-engine ValueFunction stand-in (vf, stronger than catanatron's value: about 25% vs 64%). A/A baseline and the default arm for the vf rows. 4000 games at 9390 g/h: 0.43 h.

experiments.name: t1_search_vs_heur@vf
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #2 on vf. 2000 heuristic games, estimated 0.6x a search game: 0.13 h.

experiments.name: t1_openings@vf
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #4 on vf, where the seat weakness was measured (31% of wins from seats 0-1 vs 18% from seats 2-3). standin_book is exactly the stand-ins' own opening book (mirror openings). 8000 candidate games at 0.38 s: 0.85 h.

experiments.name: t1_blockw0_pyeval@vf
experiments.notes: TIER 1 #6 on vf (Python evaluator on both arms). 4000 games at 3250 g/h: 1.23 h.

experiments.name: t2_danger_mult_off@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+2.5 +- 4.6 pp). Robber targeting by VP threat only. Changed 2/20 games vs vf in the pilot: the effect is capped by the share of games it changes (s.e. <= sqrt(f/n)). Default arm reused. 0.16 h.

experiments.name: t2_block_need0@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+1.7 +- 4.6 pp). Default 2.0; 0 switches the need bonus off. Changed 1/20 games vs vf. 0.16 h.

experiments.name: t2_turns_half2@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+0.0 +- 4.6 pp). Default 3.0. 2.0 is the value known to act vs value (changed 3/40 games in the throughput runs; 4.5 changed 0/10). 0.16 h.

experiments.name: t2_max_slack0_vrule@value
experiments.notes: POLITICS RULE (user, 2026-09-26): if this row is not significant (Holm p < 0.05) at its full seed count, label it INCONCLUSIVE, spend no more games on it (no follow-up rows, no factorial, no joint tuning) and defer it to human testing; the default stays as is. TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (-3.3 +- 4.6 pp). Favour slack 0. It only acts through trades (20/20 identical with trading off), here through search.py's trade_willingness on catanbot's own proposals. Hence --trades value: report as 'vs value-rule responders'. Default arm reused from t1_trades0_vrule@value. 1000 x 1.33 s = 0.37 h.

experiments.name: t2_coal_scale2_vrule@value
experiments.notes: POLITICS RULE (user, 2026-09-26): if this row is not significant (Holm p < 0.05) at its full seed count, label it INCONCLUSIVE, spend no more games on it (no follow-up rows, no factorial, no joint tuning) and defer it to human testing; the default stays as is. TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+0.8 / +1.7 pp for 0.25 / 1.0). Default 0.5; 2.0 makes coalition signals about 16x weaker (close to coalitions off). 20/20 identical with trading off, so run under --trades value ('vs value-rule responders'). 0.37 h.

experiments.name: t2_feed_leader_off_vrule@value
experiments.notes: POLITICS RULE (user, 2026-09-26): if this row is not significant (Holm p < 0.05) at its full seed count, label it INCONCLUSIVE, spend no more games on it (no follow-up rows, no factorial, no joint tuning) and defer it to human testing; the default stays as is. TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+0.8 +- 4.6 pp). The don't-feed-the-leader rule also drives opponent_model's prediction of who accepts catanbot's offers. 20/20 identical with trading off, so run under --trades value ('vs value-rule responders'). 0.37 h.

experiments.name: t2_knight03@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+0.8 +- 4.6 pp). Default 0.55. Changed 2/20 games vs vf. 0.16 h.

experiments.name: t2_exposure0_pyeval@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, not measured in self-play (changed 13/20 games vs vf). Needs the Python evaluator: 1960 instead of 6110 g/h (3.1x per game). It reuses the Python-evaluator default arm of t1_blockw0_pyeval@value, so only 1000 candidate games: 0.51 h (1.02 h alone, vs 0.16 h for a C++ term).

experiments.name: t2_dump0@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2, self-play showed nothing (+0.0 +- 4.6 pp). Surplus dumps with more than 7 cards off. Changed 8/20 games vs vf. 0.16 h.

experiments.name: t2_late_drop0_vrule@value
experiments.notes: POLITICS RULE (user, 2026-09-26): if this row is not significant (Holm p < 0.05) at its full seed count, label it INCONCLUSIVE, spend no more games on it (no follow-up rows, no factorial, no joint tuning) and defer it to human testing; the default stays as is. TIER 2, self-play weak signal only (+4.2 +- 4.6 pp, within noise). Trade willingness never drops late. Acts only through trades (20/20 identical with trading off), so run under --trades value ('vs value-rule responders'). 0.37 h.

experiments.name: t2x_beam2@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2 extra (not in the requested list; the harness pilot flagged it): beam 2 instead of 4, a cheaper search. Changes almost every game, so it is a place where the win rate can move. Set enabled:false to drop. 0.16 h or less.

experiments.name: t2x_expand4@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2 extra (not in the requested list; the harness pilot flagged it): expand 4 instead of 8, a cheaper search. Set enabled:false to drop. 0.16 h or less.

experiments.name: t2_steal_factor_off@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2 (user request: 'consider what resources to rob'). Off = the robber values a stolen card the same from every victim instead of by what their hand likely holds and what they / we need (danger.steal_factor, a monkeypatch flag added 2026-09-26). Acts through best_robber_move (heuristic priors, simulated opponents). Default arm reused. Not measured in self-play yet.

experiments.name: t2_rob_break_off@value
experiments.notes: TIER 2 (user request: rob the player close to winning to break their build). Off = no robber bonus for a steal that may break a near-winner's build (rob_break_probability fixed at 0). Default arm reused. Not measured in self-play yet.

experiments.name: t2_counted_info@value
experiments.notes: Cost of Colonist information: the same bot with --info counted (card counting from public events, 4 determinizations) vs the full view, paired on the same seeds. Not a strategy switch but the price of playing blind; T7 (unpaired, other seeds) gives the level. Counted mode is 3.4-4.2x per decision, so the candidate arm is slow.

experiments.name: paths_main@value
experiments.notes: Win-path portfolio with crowding (user request), Stage 3 E1 of docs/ABLATIONS_WINPATHS.md; run Stages 1-2 (calibration, shadow diagnostics, one core, ~7 min) first. Promotion also needs the league gate.

experiments.name: paths_main@vf
experiments.notes: Win-path portfolio, Stage 3 E2 (vs the 3.2.1 stand-in). Stages 4-6 (sweeps, knock-outs, held-out confirmation) follow docs/ABLATIONS_WINPATHS.md.

experiments.name: t3_search_vs_heur@alphabeta
experiments.notes: TIER 3 confirmation vs catanatron's AlphaBetaPlayer (depth 2), fresh seeds. Enable only if t1_search_vs_heur@value has Holm p < 0.05. At s.e. about 3.3 pp it confirms the direction and effects of 9 pp or more. Throughput rests on 4-6 measured games (470 g/h at 3 workers). The first enabled t3 row plays the alphabeta default arm (0.85 h); others reuse it. 1.70 h including that arm.

experiments.name: t3_trades0_vrule@alphabeta
experiments.notes: TIER 3. Enable only if t1_trades0_vrule@value has Holm p < 0.05. Answers from the value rule using alphabeta's own value function (native alphabeta raises on every offer), so this is still 'vs value-rule responders'. Own default arm (trading on). About 1.8 h.

experiments.name: t3_openings@alphabeta
experiments.notes: TIER 3. Enable only for the policies whose t1_openings@value row has Holm p < 0.05: trim 'values' to those, plus setup_pick as the control. 0.85 h per candidate (3.4 h for all four), plus 0.85 h for the default arm if no earlier t3 row played it.

experiments.name: t3_depth2@alphabeta
experiments.notes: TIER 3. Enable only if t1_depth2@value has Holm p < 0.05. About 0.96 h, plus 0.85 h for the default arm if no earlier t3 row played it.

experiments.name: t3_blockw0_pyeval@alphabeta
experiments.notes: TIER 3. Enable only if t1_blockw0_pyeval@value has Holm p < 0.05. Python evaluator on both arms, so no default reuse. About 2.1 h.
